title: Coefficient factorization of a composite twisted-pullback counit
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale derived categories and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and their constructible exceptional adjoints [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\otimes$ for $\otimes_A^L$.

Let $f:V\to W$ and $g:W\to S$ be separated finite type. Put $F_u=Ru_!$ and $P_u=Lu^*$. Choose $L_f\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$ and $L_g\in D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$, and put $L_{gf}=L_f\otimes P_fL_g$. Use the actual compact-support compositor $\alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf}$ [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the projection maps $\operatorname{PF}_{u;M,N}:F_uM\otimes N\to F_u(M\otimes P_uN)$ [def-exchange-projection]. Work on domains closed under the displayed composites, assume these projection maps are invertible there, satisfy their tensor-action identity, and satisfy
$$\operatorname{PF}_{gf;M,N}(\alpha_M\otimes1)
=\alpha_{M\otimes P_fP_gN}\,F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f;M,P_gN})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g;F_fM,N}.$$
Suppose $F_f\dashv G_f$ and $F_g\dashv G_g$ are adjunctions with $G_uK=P_uK\otimes L_u$, whose counits satisfy
$$\varepsilon_{u,K}=(1_K\otimes t_u)\Pi_{u;L_u,K},\qquad t_u=\varepsilon_{u,A},$$
with tensor-unit constraints understood and $\Pi$ the inverse projection with tensor symmetries, so $t_u:F_uL_u\to A$. Let $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}$ be the counit of the composite adjunction $F_gF_f\dashv G_fG_g$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and define
$$t_{gf}:F_{gf}L_{gf}\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}F_gF_f(L_f\otimes P_fL_g)
\xrightarrow{F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f;L_f,L_g}^{-1})}F_g(F_fL_f\otimes L_g)
\xrightarrow{F_g(t_f\otimes1)}F_gL_g\xrightarrow{t_g}A_S.$$
Then, after $G_fG_gK\cong P_{gf}K\otimes L_{gf}$ and $\alpha$, the actual composite counit is
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_K=(1_K\otimes t_{gf})\Pi_{gf;L_{gf},K}.$$
In particular $t_{gf}$ is its counit at the tensor unit. The formula is natural in $K$ on the stated domain. The same assertion holds on the ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using ordinary compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support], exact inverse image and ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the normalized compact-support comparisons [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. At that site the projection is the identical proper counit/open tensor construction; all domain assumptions and equations in the assertion are imposed on that site's actual maps.

proof.text:
Write composites right to left. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the actual composite counit before the compositor is
$$c_K=\varepsilon_{g,K}\circ F_g(\varepsilon_{f,G_gK}).$$
Put $L=L_{gf}$ and $B=P_gK$. Use the canonical tensor symmetries to write $G_uK$ as $L_u\otimes P_uK$, and put $q_{u;M,N}=\operatorname{PF}_{u;M,N}^{-1}$. The supplied factorization of each counit then reads
$$\varepsilon_{u,K}=(t_u\otimes1_K)q_{u;L_u,K}.$$
Here and below this formula includes the source symmetry and the target unit constraint. The source of $c_K$ is thereby $F_gF_f(L_f\otimes P_f(L_g\otimes B))$. Pullback's tensor comparison and the associator identify its inner argument with $L\otimes P_fB$. These are precisely the source identifications in the assertion; no adjunction different from the supplied one is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, equation-compose-counits; substitution F=F_f, H=F_g, G=G_f, I=G_g

proof.text:
Invert the assumed tensor-action identity for $f$ and substitute $M=L_f$, $N_1=L_g$, $N_2=B$. With the preceding pullback/tensor identifications it gives
$$q_{f;L_f,L_g\otimes B}=(q_{f;L_f,L_g}\otimes1_B)q_{f;L,B}.$$
Define the particular morphism
$$a=(t_f\otimes1_{L_g})q_{f;L_f,L_g}:F_fL\longrightarrow L_g.$$
Substituting the supplied formula for $\varepsilon_{f,G_gK}$ and using bifunctoriality of tensor now gives
$$\varepsilon_{f,G_gK}=(a\otimes1_B)q_{f;L,B}.$$
The first equality is just the inverse of the hypothesis, and the second composes $t_f$ with its first tensor factor. Both formulas have domain $F_f(L\otimes P_fB)$ and codomain $L_g\otimes B$ in the second case.

proof.text:
Substitute the preceding equality and the supplied formula for $\varepsilon_{g,K}$ into $c_K$. Functoriality of $F_g$ gives the equality
$$c_K=(t_g\otimes1_K)q_{g;L_g,K}\,F_g(a\otimes1_B)\,F_g(q_{f;L,B}).$$
In particular $F_g(q_{f;L,B})$ ends at $F_g(F_fL\otimes P_gK)$, $F_g(a\otimes1_B)$ ends at $F_g(L_g\otimes P_gK)$, and $q_{g;L_g,K}$ ends at $F_gL_g\otimes K$. Thus every displayed factor is on the domains assumed closed under these composites.

proof.text:
The projection maps of [def-exchange-projection] are natural transformations in their two inputs; their inverses on the stated domain are therefore natural too (multiply the naturality square on both sides by the inverses). Apply this naturality in the first input to $a:F_fL\to L_g$:
$$q_{g;L_g,K}F_g(a\otimes1_{P_gK})=(F_g(a)\otimes1_K)q_{g;F_fL,K}.$$
Consequently Step 3 simplifies, by tensor bifunctoriality, to
$$c_K=(t_gF_g(a)\otimes1_K)q_{g;F_fL,K}F_g(q_{f;L,P_gK}).$$
Naturality supplies exactly this square, not an identification inferred only from an equality at $K=A_S$.

proof.text:
Invert the projection/compositor identity assumed in the statement, and multiply by the compositor inverses. At $M=L$ this gives
$$q_{g;F_fL,K}F_g(q_{f;L,P_gK})\alpha_{L\otimes P_fP_gK}^{-1}
=(\alpha_L^{-1}\otimes1_K)q_{gf;L,K}.$$
Indeed inverting the hypothesis first gives $\alpha_L\otimes1_K=\operatorname{PF}_{gf;L,K}^{-1}\alpha_{L\otimes P_fP_gK}F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f;L,P_gK})\operatorname{PF}_{g;F_fL,K}$, and cancellation of its three right-hand invertible factors gives the displayed equality. Precompose Step 4 by $\alpha_{L\otimes P_fP_gK}^{-1}$ and use it:
$$c_K\alpha^{-1}=(t_gF_g(a)\alpha_L^{-1}\otimes1_K)q_{gf;L,K}=(t_{gf}\otimes1_K)q_{gf;L,K}.$$
The last equality expands the definition of $a$, giving exactly the four arrows defining $t_{gf}$ in the statement. Finally insert the source symmetry $P_{gf}K\otimes L\cong L\otimes P_{gf}K$ and the target symmetry $F_{gf}L\otimes K\cong K\otimes F_{gf}L$. Naturality of the latter symmetry changes $t_{gf}\otimes1_K$ into $1_K\otimes t_{gf}$, so this is the claimed formula with $\Pi_{gf;L,K}$.

proof.text: Take $K=A_S$. With pullback's unit comparison and the tensor unitors, $q_{gf;L,A_S}$ is the identity. One can check this from the assumed action law alone: specialize it to $N_1=N_2=A_S$ and identify $L\otimes P_{gf}A_S$ with $L$; it says $q=q^2$. Since $q$ is invertible, cancellation gives $q=1$. Thus Step 5 at the unit is $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_{A_S}=t_{gf}$ under the same compositor and unit identifications.

proof.text: Every expression used in Steps 1--5 is natural in $K$: the counits and compositor are natural, $P_f,P_g,F_f,F_g$ are functors, and $q$ is the inverse of the natural projection transformation [def-exchange-projection]. More explicitly, for $h:K\to K'$ its naturality in the second input gives $(1_{F_{gf}L}\otimes h)q_{gf;L,K}=q_{gf;L,K'}F_{gf}(1_L\otimes P_{gf}h)$; composition with $t_{gf}$ and the two symmetries gives the claimed naturality square. The calculation has used only the stated adjunctions, tensor action, naturality and projection/compositor equation. For ordinary etale categories repeat Steps 1--6 with their own functors, adjunctions, compositor and projection maps. The assertion expressly imposes the same identities and closure assumptions on those actual maps, so each displayed substitution has the same type there. This proves the ordinary-site clause without identifying the two sites or transferring an unproved projection identity between them.
